sections.skill: Calculate how discounts and refunds change contribution and write a policy

questions.prompt: A 25-dollar item costs 15 dollars. With a 20 percent discount, what is the new price?
questions.intro: Discounts and refunds reduce what a sale brings in, often more than people expect. A 20 percent discount on a 25-dollar item with a 15-dollar cost cuts the contribution from 10 dollars to 5 dollars: half the money from that sale. A REFUND gives money back; the item may come back damaged or not at all, and some processors do not return their fee. Write a clear refund policy (time limit, condition of returns, who pays shipping) and post it before customers buy.

questions.prompt: What is 50 with 20 percent off?
questions.intro: To take a percent off, multiply by (1 - the decimal). 20 percent off means multiply by 0.80; 15 percent off means multiply by 0.85. Example: 40 dollars with 25 percent off: 40 x 0.75 = 30 dollars. Or find the discount first: 0.25 x 40 = 10, then 40 - 10 = 30. Both ways give the same answer.
